summary: Android background voice acceptance did not distinguish muted listener continuity from continuing microphone capture. The app's foreground service currently declares only mediaProjection; Android requires a microphone foreground-service type for background microphone capture on supported target levels.

checks.name: Current Android service declaration
checks.observation: The IsolateHolderService declares foregroundServiceType=mediaProjection. The app manifest does not declare FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MICROPHONE.

checks.name: MediaProjection foreground-service readiness contract
checks.observation: The focused Flutter test passed: screen capture waits for the MediaProjection foreground service. This covers projection readiness, not background microphone capture.

checks.name: Background voice test coverage
checks.observation: The recorded Pixel background reproduction had the microphone disabled; it cannot establish whether an active microphone continues when BOOHTACORD is backgrounded.

checks.name: Android platform requirements
checks.observation: For Android 14+ targets, microphone capture in an FGS requires the microphone service type, FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MICROPHONE, and RECORD_AUDIO; an FGS requiring while-in-use microphone access must be started while a visible activity is present.

limitations: This is a source/spec gap, not a reproduced device failure or proof that the existing muted-session participant loss was caused by microphone service configuration.
No Android permission, service type, or runtime behavior was changed.
remaining: On an authenticated Pixel test session, separately verify background voice with the microphone muted and enabled. If active microphone continuity is part of the intended Android parity, review ADR-006 and implement/test a properly timed microphone foreground service before claiming acceptance.
